text:
sara (Sales): Hey team — ModuWare wants to run a short POC. They built a custom variant 'orca-mini-12b-quant' and want to test on Dedicated/A100. Main asks: token pricing for ~1M tokens/mo on reserved, KV/prefix cache compatibility, and any blockers for Private VPC + KMS. cc @mike_ml @tess_ops @priya_sec

mike_ml (Eng-ML): Quick q — what are their typical prompt + response lengths? latency SLOs? that affects batching/quant tradeoffs.

sara (Sales): Mostly short prompts (user ~40 tokens) with 200 token responses avg. They want p95 < 300ms for simple completions.

mike_ml (Eng-ML): OK. With A100 reserved we can probably hit that with int8 quant if we enable continuous batching + prefix KV cache. Need to confirm model ops because some quantized variants change kernel path. Can we get their model wheel or a sample checkpoint?

tess_ops (Solutions): I'll ask ModuWare for a checkpoint. Also confirm whether they need persistent KV cache across requests or just prefix caching per session — that changes memory footprint.

sara (Sales): They said persistent within a session is fine, don't need cross-session persistence.

mike_ml (Eng-ML): Good. That should be compatible with our KV cache primitives. Example config I'd run on Dedicated for a quick smoke: 
```yaml
model: orca-mini-12b-quant
precision: int8
hardware: a100-80gb
batching:
  max_tokens_per_batch: 4096
  latency_target_ms: 250
kv_cache: prefix_only
max_sequence_length: 2048
```

mike_ml (Eng-ML): Two notes: 1) if their quant variant uses a nonstandard RMSNorm op we may need to swap kernels or fallback to a compatible build. 2) Throughput/price depends on avg concurrency — what concurrency should we assume for 1M tokens/mo?

sara (Sales): They expect ~30 concurrent users at peak, but most traffic is bursty. Pricing question was about hosted token-equivalent vs reserved. Any ballpark numbers?

tess_ops (Solutions): For Dedicated reserved capacity we'd quote a monthly pool price + effective per-token internal accounting. Ballpark: current avg for similar 12B quant variants on A100 pool we see $0.004–0.01 per 1k tokens depending on utilization and batch hit rate. I'll run numbers once we know concurrency and KV hit rate.

priya_sec (Security): From a security perspective: Private VPC + KMS is fine. We need completed security questionnaire + confirmation they don't require on-prem air-gapped. Also need list of data retention expectations and whether they plan to send PHI. If PHI, we escalate to compliance for contract addendum.

sara (Sales): They said no PHI, just product data. I'll send the questionnaire. Is there anything in-platform that would block KMS usage?

priya_sec (Security): No platform blockers. We'll need a KMS key policy template and ensure logs are forwarded to their log collector if requested. Also request for key rotations frequency.

mike_ml (Eng-ML): If they can share a small validation corpus (20–50 prompts) I can run evals on a staging node to verify perf and quality regression against our baseline. That will catch weird op/kernel issues early.

sara (Sales): OK I'll ask for the checkpoint + 50 prompts. I already opened a ticket for infra staging.

deploy-bot: Ticket #INC-2026 created: "moduware-poc-staging-request" assigned to eng-ml and eng-infra. ETA: 48h. :spiral_calendar_pad:

tess_ops (Solutions): Next steps: 1) ModuWare shares checkpoint + prompts + concurrency pattern. 2) Eng-ML runs staging validation and reports kernel/compat issues. 3) Solutions runs cost calc and drafts reserved quote. 4) Security completes the questionnaire and KMS checklist. We'll sync in 48h. :thumbsup:

sara (Sales): Thanks — I'll update ModuWare and post replies here.

priya_sec (Security): If they need faster turnaround on the security questionnaire, have them mark it high priority and share the attacker surface doc. Otherwise normal SLA applies.

mike_ml (Eng-ML): One more thing — ask if the model was exported from pipelines that include fused ops (e.g., custom fused attention). If so, we'll need the original export config.

sara (Sales): noted. sending list of asks to ModuWare now.
